title: Taranga 13. Srinivasa Acharya's Marriage and Other Events
html:
Farewell to Navadvipa and Shrikhanda; Vira Hambira at Yajigrama; the Deity of Sri Radhika sent by Jahnava, at Kantaka-nagara; Kheturi; Raghunandana's departure; Srinivasa's second marriage; the Deity of Radhika beside Gopinatha in Vrindavana; Virachandra and Gangadevi; Virachandra's journey to Vraja: the circuit of the forests, Radha-kunda, Govardhana, Radhashtami; the return

1Glory, glory to Sri Krishna Chaitanya, the refuge of all!
Glory, glory to the merciful Lord Nityananda!

2Glory to Sri Advaita-deva, the ocean of virtues!
Glory, glory to Srivasa Pandita, to Gadadhara!

3Glory to Gadadhara Dasa, to Sri Murari Gupta!
Glory to Vakreshvara, to Sri Mukunda, to Narahari!

4Glory to Sri Pandita Gauridasa, to Damodara!
Glory to Svarupa, to Haridasa, to Shuklambara!

5Glory, glory to all the devotees of the Lord!
Show mercy, all of you — I have taken shelter [of you].

6Glory, glory to the listeners, the abode of virtues!
Now with kind hearts listen to what I shall tell.

7Srinivasa Acharya, Narottama and Ramachandra
found great bliss in wandering through Navadvipa.

8Having bowed at the feet of Sri Ishana Thakura,
at the parting their hearts are breaking.

9Sri Ishana Thakura, embracing [them],
lost his composure — his tears could not be stopped.

10In a rush of tenderness his body grew utterly powerless;
who can understand his deep heart?

11He wishes to say something but cannot speak;
with a sign of the hand he made known: the meeting — from this [the last].1

12Those associates of the Lord who were there —
the hearts of all of them became greatly distressed.

13Showing great favor, they gave [them] leave;
then Sri Acharya bowed at the feet of them all.

14Bowing again and again to Navadvipa-dhama,
weeping, weeping, they go, having taken leave.

15On the way, wherever there were homes of devotees,
going there and there, they were filled with joy.

16Coming to Shrikhanda, they had darshan of Gauranga;
there was a meeting with Sri Raghunandana.

17Sri Raghunandana, in a great rush of tenderness,
gently asks about Navadvipa.

18Srinivasa, having told of the wandering through Nadia,
speaks of the devotees, weeping, weeping.

19"Before, many devotees in Nadia withdrew from sight;
those who remain now are almost all in mauna-mudra.2

20In the Lord's house Ishana alone abides;
his endless virtues — what power have I to tell them?

21Coming along the road, I heard from people's mouths:
Sri Ishana Thakura has withdrawn from sight.3

22Day by day Nadia is sinking into darkness;
what can I say — I do not know what more will happen."

23At what was heard prema surges, patience cannot hold;
Srinivasa, clasping [him] by the neck, weeps aloud.

24By the Lord's will after some time [they] grew calm;
the state of Sri Raghunandana — who knows how to describe it?

25Consoling Srinivasa in many ways,
he gave [them] leave to go to Yajigrama.

26The three, bowing to Sri Raghunandana,
went to Yajigrama, taking courage.

27Sri Gokulananda and others, with great joy in their minds,
came forward to meet them and took them to the house.

28The people of Yajigrama, with joyful hearts,
came to the Acharya's house and had darshan.

29Srinivasa Acharya Thakura met with all of them,
as befitted each, with a joyful heart.

30Wonderful is the character of Srinivasa Acharya:
he gladdened the minds of all in every way.

31Outside the house was a very secluded place;
there he sat, taking everyone with him.

32Overwhelmed by the talk of Navadvipa,
he asked one by one about the welfare of his disciples.

33To dear Narottama he says very softly:
"I feel that Vira Hambira will come today."4

34Just then a man sent by the king
announced: "The king will arrive today."

35Meanwhile King Sri Vira Hambira, with joy in his mind,
comes from Vana-Vishnupura at an auspicious moment.

36At the sight of Yajigrama his joy is boundless;
stopping at a distance, the king bows to Yajigrama.

37Seeing a beautiful place near Yajigrama,
he decided to stop there to rest.

38Leaving there the horses, elephants, foot soldiers and the rest,
he enters the village, taking a few people with him.

39All the provisions he had brought from home
he sent first of all to the Prabhu's house.5

40Remembering the feet of Sri Acharya Prabhu,
very slowly he walks to where the Acharya's house is.

41Beholding the lotus feet of Acharya Prabhu,
he bows again and again, falling to the ground.

42Seeing Narottama's radiance, he reasons in his mind:
"This prabhu is surely Thakura Mahashaya.

43I have attained the goal" — saying this, in unceasing joy
he bows again and again at Narottama's feet.

44Sri Acharya Thakura and Thakura Narottama,
showing great favor, embraced [him].

45Bowing at the feet of Ramachandra Kaviraja,
he requests: "Make me acquainted with the prabhus."

46Ramachandra, the abode of virtues, in joy
made known [to him] who was who among the Prabhu's associates.

47The king in great joy falls to the ground to bow;
all embraced him, overwhelmed with prema.

48The joy in the heart of King Vira Hambira —
what do I know to tell it? Such is the manifestation of bhakti.

49The people of Yajigrama, with joyful hearts,
seeing the king's devotion, praise the king.

50All the attendants of King Vira Hambira —
all have the right to the pure path of bhakti.

51The good fortune of the king with his people has no limit;
all extol [it] to one another here and there.

52Sri Acharya Thakura and Thakura Mahashaya,
seeing the king's conduct, rejoice beyond measure.

53Acharya Thakura, looking at Ramachandra,
entrusted Sri Vira Hambira to him.

54Whatever arose in Vira Hambira's mind,
about that he asks Ramachandra Kaviraja.

55How the ishta-goshthi of these two is known everywhere —
the author has described in detail in another book.6

56The king — at the sight of his own Prabhu's dear ones —
who can tell what bliss there is in Yajigrama!

57To stay in Yajigrama — such is the king's wish;
moment by moment in Yajigrama [his] great yearning grows.

58The king has no wish to go to Vishnupura;
Ramachandra made [this] known to the Acharya.

59Acharya Thakura and Sri Thakura Mahashaya
in a rush of tenderness console Sri Vira Hambira.

60Consoling [him], giving him people as companions, at that very moment
they sent [him] to see the places worshiped by all.

61The king, utterly humble, went round everywhere;
by the grace of all the mahantas he was filled with joy.

62Coming to Yajigrama, he reflects in his mind:
"How shall I go to Vishnupura without the Prabhu?"

63Knowing the king's heart, Acharya Thakura
speaks sweet words to the king:

64"Some days from now, after going to the village of Kheturi,
I shall come here from there and go to Vishnupura.

65From Khardaha Sri Jahnava Ishvari
will send news — I am waiting, watching the road."

66Even as he was saying this, someone with joy in his heart
came from Khardaha to the Acharya.

67Seeing him, the Acharya rejoiced in heart;
with the sweetest words he asks about [his] welfare.

68He, very humbly, in a soft voice,
briefly reports to Sri Acharya:

69"In Khardaha all is well; Sri Ishvari,
showing mercy to the living beings, distributes prema-bhakti.

70Having had a Sri Deity of Radhika made,
she became greatly overwhelmed, gazing at Her beauty.7

71To Sri Parameshvari Dasa and other wise ones
she gave the order to take [Her] to Vrindavana.

72She gave seven hundred coins, garments, ornaments and more;
with care they placed [Her] on a wonderful boat.

73Remembering Sri Gopinatha, she says:
'Quickly draw Your beloved to Yourself.'

74Who else could understand Sri Ishvari's doings?
At a most auspicious moment she sent [them] on their way.

75Once sent off, the boat came swiftly;
it stopped for only one day in Nadia.

76Today the boat will arrive at Kantaka-nagara;
taking the letter, I hurried here."

77Saying this, he gave the letter into the Acharya's hand;
the Acharya took the letter and placed it on his head.

78As soon as he read the letter, with great joy in his heart,
he sets out with everyone for Sri Kantaka-nagara.

79The clothes, ornaments and other things that had been prepared
he took with him, in order to present them.

80A thousand coins Vira Hambira secretly
gave to Sri Ramachandra Kaviraja.

81Ramachandra told Acharya Prabhu [of it];
smiling, the Acharya took them with him.

82He quickly arrived at Kantaka-nagara
and came to the ghat of Sri Keshava Bharati Gosani.8

83He sees: at that very moment the boat came to that ghat;
great bliss arose as they met one another.

84Sri Parameshvari Dasa, Nrisimha Chaitanya,
Thakura Kanai and others, accomplished in every way —9

85who can understand the hearts of them all?
Meeting Sri Acharya, their happiness grew beyond measure.

86When the Acharya spoke of Sri Navadvipa,
all became distraught — no one could remain composed.

87Srinivasa Acharya and the others were agitated at heart;
after a while all, full of prema, became composed.

88The king, falling at the feet of all — Sri Parameshvari Dasa
and everyone else — bowed to them.

89Everyone, learning who the king was,
showed him great mercy, embracing him tightly.

90Seeing the radiance of them all, Sri Vira Hambira,
in the bliss of prema, lost his composure — he cannot be still.

91The people of Kantaka-nagara, seeing prema arise,
all praise the king's good fortune.

92Who does not weep, hearing of the king's humility?
Nrisimha Chaitanya says to the king, "Blessed [are you]."

93Someone says, "The Acharya's mercy is powerful:
by this bond the king is to us like life itself."

94Everyone's wondrous affection for the king grew;
how can I tell what feelings arise in the king?

95Sri Parameshvari Dasa Thakura joyfully
led Acharya Srinivasa onto the boat.

96He speaks sweet words to the Acharya:
"Sri Ishvari will go to Vrindavana again.10

97Having offered Sri Radhika to Sri Gopinatha,
we will soon come [back] by boat."

98Saying this, he removed the cloth covering
and showed [him] the Sri Deity of Radhika.

99Beautiful in every limb — no comparison can be given;
seeing [Her], the Acharya was utterly overwhelmed with prema.

100Then Sri Parameshvari Dasa, with joy in his heart,
shows the Acharya all the gifts.

101"Gopinatha and Sri Gopinatha's two beloveds —
these are the clothes, ornaments and other things for these three.

102To the Lords — Sri Govinda, Madanamohana —
I will offer these clothes and ornaments, each in his own place."

103Thus he showed everything, each thing separately;
seeing it, the Acharya's great joy kept growing.

104Some clothes and ornaments and a thousand coins
the Acharya presented with great humility.

105Sri Parameshvari Dasa, with the greatest affection,
brought everyone onto the boat and gave them darshan.

106Narottama, Ramachandra, Govinda, Shridasa,
Gokulananda and all the others rejoice at the darshan.

107On the bank of the Ganga a great crowd of people gathered;
seeing the beauty of the Vaishnavas, how much they say in joy!

108After staying for some time on the bank of the Ganga, everyone
set out for the darshan of "Gauranga."11

109Sri Yadunandana and others, in great joy,
led everyone to the courtyard of Sri Gauranga.

110Having the darshan of "Gauranga," everyone
lost their composure — the tears could not be stopped.

111In the courtyard of "Gauranga" the ocean of prema surged;
all became intoxicated in the sankirtana of the Holy Name.

112The sound of the kirtana of the Holy Name pierces the sky;
Nrisimha Chaitanya dances wonderfully.

113In the rapture of prema Parameshvari Dasa says,
"Sing, sing, O Narottama, Srinivasa!"

114Thakura Kanai cannot be still;
he embraces Ramachandra again and again.

115Shridasa, Gokulananda, Govinda and all the others
became maddened in the kirtana of the Holy Name.

116Sankirtana is the very treasure of the Lord's dear ones;
whom does sankirtana not attract?

117Having drunk the nectar of the sankirtana of the Name for some time,
everyone grew calm in the courtyard of "Gauranga."

118Where the Lord accepted sannyasa,
there everyone became covered with dust.

119How can I tell of the ways of these prabhus?
That day they stayed in Kantaka-nagara.

120As soon as night turned to dawn,
they took leave of one another, their hearts in great distress.

121Sri Parameshvari Dasa and the others, having said much,
departed from Kantaka-nagara with the boat.

122Srinivasa Acharya, taking his dear ones,
came from Kantaka-nagara to Yajigrama.

123Matchless is the Acharya's affection for his disciple;
"I must bid farewell to the king" — at this his sorrow is great.

124Sri Vira Hambira is to go to Vishnupura;
at the parting his heart cannot find steadiness.

125Holding the lotus feet of Acharya Prabhu on his head,
with tears he speaks slowly and softly:

126"Come quickly to Vana-Vishnupura
and take [us] under your protection, looking on [us] with a merciful glance."

127Embracing him, Acharya Thakura says,
"There will be no delay in coming to Vishnupura."

128Hearing this, [the king] falls at Narottama's feet;
he bathes his two lotus feet with the tears of his eyes.

129"Be merciful," he says in a choked voice.
"In all the three worlds there is no offender like me.

130Because of my wicked deed you suffered at heart;
when I think of all that, I do not know what my heart is doing."12

131Hearing this, Thakura Mahashaya says,
"From that wicked deed came victory everywhere.

132Now keep all that in mind no longer;
be diligent in acquiring the jewel of bhakti."

133Saying much like this, he embraced him tightly;
the king's mind became filled with great joy.

134He bows at the feet of Ramachandra and Govinda;
hearing of the humility he shows, the heart melts.

135At the feet of both, Shridasa and Gokulananda,
the king bows, and tears stream from his eyes.

136To all the disciples of Sri Acharya Prabhu,
one after another, he bowed at their feet.

137Bowing to the people of Yajigrama,
the king took leave, overcome with distress.

138The king's queen, with great joy in her heart,
was inside Sri Acharya's house.

139The Acharya's wife is named Draupadi Ishvari;13
she is full of every virtue, of wondrous charm.

140The queen had brought clothes and ornaments;
dressing her in them, she sees a marvellous beauty.

141The queen placed her two feet on her own head;
at the parting she became greatly distressed.

142Bowing again and again to the ground of Yajigrama,
the queen departed, riding in a palanquin.

143The king, having gone some distance from Yajigrama,
mounted a splendid carriage and went to Vana-Vishnupura.

144The next day Sri Acharya Thakura
went to Khanda with Narottama and Ramachandra.14

145Bowing to Sri Raghunandana, he requests,
"Tomorrow morning I will go to Kheturi — please give your permission."

146Sri Raghunandana says, "Go to Kheturi;
stay there a few days, then come back quickly."

147Having said this, he gave the Acharya leave;
coming to Yajigrama, all ponder in their hearts.

148Acharya Thakura says to Narottama:
"The Thakura has never given such an order.15

149Who is able to understand the doings of Chaitanya's associates?
I do not know when he will plunge [everything] into darkness."16

150As soon as he said this, tears streamed from his eyes;
having lost his composure, after some time he grew calm.

151Acharya Thakura, quickly taking everyone with him,
came from Yajigrama to Kanchanagariya.

152There they stayed for two days,
immersed day and night in the bliss of sankirtana.

153They set out from the village of Kanchanagariya
and came to the vicinity of the village of Budhari.

154The residents of Budhari, with great joy in their hearts,
came forward to meet them and brought them to a wonderful house.

155Sri Acharya Thakura, Thakura Mahashaya,
Ramachandra and the others were overjoyed.

156Sri Acharya Thakura, with supreme bliss in his heart,
was intoxicated with sankirtana day and night.

157Having stayed two days in the village of Budhari,
they crossed the Padmavati and went to Kheturi.

158The residents of Sri Kheturi, with great joy in their hearts,
led them from the bank of the Padmavati.

159Entering the village of Kheturi, everyone
with joy in their hearts had darshana of the Lord.

160Having stayed some time in the Lord's courtyard,
everyone went to their own lodgings.

161All the fortunate people who live in Kheturi
in the bliss of darshana know neither day nor night.

162Sri Acharya Thakura and Thakura Mahashaya
revel day and night in the bliss of sankirtana.

163Whom do they not immerse in the ocean of bhakti-rasa?
Who does not sing of the wonderful mercy of these two?

164The deeds of Srinivasa and Narottama, these two,
become known everywhere day by day.

165One day a great, invincible pashanda,
seeing the two in sankirtana, was amazed.

166That brahmana from Bengal, floating in tears,
fell at the feet of the two, rolling [on the ground].

167The brahmana, a disputant and a worldly man, became full of bhakti;
he took shelter of the lotus feet of Sri Acharya.

168The Acharya entrusted him to Narottama, [his very] life;
everyone rejoiced at his fitness for bhakti.

169Such play the Acharya and Narottama reveal;
who can understand the unfathomable nature of these two?

170One day the Acharya, taking Sri Narottama with him,
said something to him in solitude and became distraught.

171Having stayed only a very few days, he took leave
and with his companions hurried back to Yajigrama.

172The Thakura went to Raghunandana;17
in a rush of affection he embraced Srinivasa.

173Asking about his welfare, holding Srinivasa's hand,
sitting in solitude, he says something very softly:

174"A time is coming — in it things will be hard:
in everyone's heart various doubts will arise."

175Thus [it is said] in the Sri Bhajanamrita:18
"When Krishna Chaitanya-chandra and Nityananda have concluded Their descent in this [age of] Kali,
all the Vaishnavas indeed

176will always be anxious; as time goes on, day by day,
almost all — the highest, the lowest and the middling — will become doubtful at heart."

177"Do not be anxious about this: Lord Gaura-raya
will accomplish many works through you.

178You will live long on the earth
and together with your companions will preserve the Lord's dharma.

179By your power those who have turned away from Krishna
will turn [to Him], taking shelter of you."

180Thus, having said many things, he consoled Srinivasa
and went before Madana-gopala and Gauranga.

181Entrusting his son to the feet of Gaura and Gopala,
for three days he was in great rapture in sankirtana.

182Remembering the lotus feet of Narahari,19
he fixed his eyes on the forms of Gopala and Gauranga.

183Uttering the name of Sri Krishna Chaitanya again and again,
he disappeared; seeing this, the people were astonished.

184Blessed is that day — the fourth day of the bright fortnight of Shravana!20
Who does not sing the glory of Raghunandana?

185Sri Raghunandana's son, Thakura Kanai,
made preparations for a festival to which there was no end.

186Srinivasa Acharya stayed in Khanda
until the great festival was completed.

187There was a festival such as cannot be described;
all the mahantas came to Khanda.

188Acharya Thakura is wise in all arrangements;
what can I say of the bliss that was in the sankirtana?

189Sri Thakura Kanai's son is Sri Madana;
he too danced wonderfully in the sankirtana.

190Who can tell the qualities of Madana?
Since the occasion has come, I will tell a little, in few words.

191In Kanai's youth two sons were born to him one after the other —21
Sri Madana and Vamshi, full of bhakti-rasa.

192Madana in the age of pauganda revealed the jewel of bhakti;
he surrendered himself at the feet of Prabhu Narahari.

193Seeing him, all people attain great bliss;
his dancing and kirtana — who knows how to describe them?

194What shall I say of how prema was revealed in Shrikhanda!
Whatever desire anyone had was fulfilled.

195All the mahantas went to their own homes;
Srinivasa Acharya was given leave with loving care.

196Hearing what Thakura Kanai said at the parting,22
Srinivasa floats in tears.

197Remembering the qualities of Sri Raghunandana,
he came to Yajigrama, weeping and weeping.

198Having stayed four days in Yajigrama, the Acharya
went very quickly to Vana-Vishnupura.

199The king with his family, with great joy in his heart,
came forward to meet him and led Acharya Thakura [to his place].

200In Vishnupura the Acharya has a wonderful residence;
the Acharya with his companions arrived there.

201All the greatly fortunate residents of Vishnupura
are beside themselves day and night at the darshana of the Acharya.

202One day Sri Acharya Thakura in a dream
marries by the order of Gaurachandra.

203This is most wonderful; I will tell in brief
how the Acharya's second marriage came about.

204In the land of Rarh there is a village named Gopalpura;23
the community of brahmanas there is exceedingly distinguished.

205In that village is the house of the brahmana Raghunatha;
some call him Sri Raghava Chakravarti.

206The brahmana's wife is named Sri Madhavi;
their daughter is Sri Gauranga-priya, of virtuous conduct.24

207The daughter's match is never settled;
in the hearts of the brahmana and his wife there is great anxiety.

208One day at dawn the lady
speaks sweet words to her husband:

209"In a dream a brahmana, a great Arya, told me:
'The husband of your daughter is Srinivasa Acharya.'

210When I courteously asked where he had come from,
he said, 'I have come from Shantipura.'25

211As I was going to ask something more, my sleep broke;
the radiance I saw filled my heart."

212The brahmana says, "At dawn I [too] saw a dream:
I gave my daughter to Srinivasa Acharya."

213Hearing this, the brahmana's wife says, "Why delay any longer?26
Go there — he will surely consent."

214At his wife's words the brahmana rejoiced at heart;
he went quickly and put [the matter] before the Acharya.

215Hearing this, the Acharya remained silent;
to satisfy the hearts of all, he married.

216All the people say again and again, "Blessed, blessed!
As the bride is, so is the groom — a wonderful beauty!"

217The king with his family is exceedingly joyful;
he spent much wealth on the Acharya's wedding.

218Having stayed some days in Vishnupura, the Acharya,
consoling everyone, came to Yajigrama.

219The Acharya goes with everyone to his home;
the villagers watch with joy in their hearts.

220The Acharya's two wives, both gazing at each other —
their hearts overflow with the natural bliss of love.

221Their loving endeavors cannot be described;
they are always overwhelmed by the joy of serving the Acharya.

222The Acharya delights in the bliss of love for Sri Krishna
and distributes to his disciples the jewels of books on bhakti.

223One day the Acharya says to his disciples:
"Suddenly joy is arising in my mind.

224Sri Parameshvari Dasa and the other prabhus —
perhaps today they will all arrive here."

225As soon as he said this, Sri Parameshvari Dasa
appeared in the distance — Srinivasa saw [him].

226The Acharya Thakura went out to meet them with everyone;
the honor he showed was beyond words.

227Seating Sri Parameshvari Dasa and all [with him]
on splendid seats, he asks about their welfare.

228Sri Parameshvari Dasa speaks slowly:
"Without hindrance we went quickly to Vrindavana.

229Gopinatha gave the command to His servitor,
and the one we had brought, [the servitor] seated on the left.27

230The former Thakurani joyfully sat on the right;28
a wondrous beauty appeared — I saw [it] with my own eyes.

231O Srinivasa! No one could remain composed,
seeing Gopinatha on the throne with His beloved ones.

232They say to one another, 'Look, what a wondrous appearance!
Radhika, sent by Sri Jahnava, is at the left side.'

233Saying this, they sing the virtues of Jahnava Ishvari
and proclaim her glory — who, hearing [it], would not be gladdened?

234And again all, in order to see Ishvari,
pray, gazing at the face of Gopinatha.

235The longing of the people cannot be told;
with fixed gaze they look at Sri Radhika.

236'Radhika, installed by Sri Jahnava' — saying this,
the people move here and there, rejoicing.

237Having seen the great festival there,
we all came here entirely without hindrance.

238Today we shall board a boat at Kantaka-nagara
and soon make this news known at Khardaha.

239Sri Ishvari will soon go there again —
I told you as well: it was spoken of before."

240Hearing this, Sri Acharya was greatly delighted
and came with everyone to Sri Kantaka-nagara.

241Sri Parameshvari and the others boarded the boat;
having said much to Srinivasa, they took their leave.

242Sri Parameshvari and the others went to Khardaha
and bowed at the holy feet of Sri Vasu[dha] and Jahnava.

243They told everything; hearing it, Jahnava Ishvari
was absorbed in prema in a way I cannot describe.

244Who can understand the mind of Ishvari?
She says softly to Sri Parameshvari Dasa:

245"Go quickly to the village of Tada-Atpur
and manifest there the service of Radha-Gopinatha."29

246By the command of Ishvari, Sri Parameshvari Dasa
manifested the service of Radha-Gopinatha.

247Sri Ishvari went to that place;
the festival that took place there the fortunate saw.

248Whatever villages Ishvari went to —
the good fortune of all those villages cannot be described.

249To Jhamatpur near Rajbalhat
Ishvari went, to the house of a servant.30

250There lives the brahmana Yadunandana Acharya;
by the mercy of Ishvari he became full of bhakti.31

251Yadunandana's wife is named Lakshmi;
what to say — hers is the utmost dharma of a chaste wife.

252He has two daughters — Shrimati and Narayani;
the grace of their limbs is the utmost limit of beauty.32

253By the wish of Sri Ishvari that fortunate brahmana
gave both daughters to Prabhu Virachandra.

254At the time of the wedding there was great festivity;
Virachandra made Yadunandana [his] disciple.

255Jahnava Ishvari, greatly rejoicing,
made Shrimati and Sri Narayani — both — [her] disciples.

256The fortunate saw Virachandra's wedding;
who could describe the splendor of that wedding?

257Nityananda's son, full of great splendor,
his body non-different from Chaitanya, enchanting the world.

258Thus [it is said] in the Sri Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika:
He who is the vyuha of Sankarshana named Payodhishayi —
he himself appeared as Virachandra, his form non-different from Chaitanya.33

259Having married, Virachandra came home;
seeing her daughters-in-law, Vasu[dha] was filled with great joy.

260In the village of Khardaha everyone rejoiced;
the wedding gifts that were given were beyond reckoning.

261At her brother's wedding Gangadevi was overjoyed;
what power have I to tell the virtues of Sri Gangadevi?

262The festivity that took place at her own auspicious wedding
is known everywhere — who could tell how much [there was]?

263Gangadevi is the Ganga born from the feet of Vishnu;
her husband is Madhava Acharya, full of bhakti.

264Thus [it is said] in the Sri Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika:
The Ganga born from the feet of Vishnu — she who [was so called] by her own name as well —
was born as the daughter of Nityananda; and Madhava is King Shantanu.34

265Thus [it is said] in the Sri Vaishnava-vandana:
"I shall praise Madhava Acharya, full of the bliss of love,
who by the power of bhakti became the husband of Gangadevi."

266The joy that [was] in Khardaha cannot be told;
who does not sing the deeds of Virachandra?

267Jahnava Ishvari arranged her son's marriage
and made the poor and lowly fit for bhakti.

268Again she quickly went with her companions to Vrindavana
and beheld Gopinatha together with Radha.

269In the middle is Gopinatha, Radha on the right and the left;
the wise describe that wondrous beauty in many ways.

270Thus [it is said] in the Stavamrita-lahari composed by Sri Vishvanatha Chakravarti:
Is it a tamala tree [standing] amid creepers of prema?
Is it a cloud lit by lightning on both sides?
Or is it, between the two Radhas, the dark moon —
Gopinatha of the broad chest, our refuge?35

271What power have I to describe the grace of Sri Gopinatha?
That embodiment of love is subject to the prema of Sri Jahnava.

272Thus [it is said] in the same [work]:
The embodied treasure of Sri Jahnava's prema,
showing Himself to the poor and helpless, gracious,
nourishing [them] with the nectar of remnants unattainable even by the gods —
Gopinatha of the broad chest is our refuge.36

273What Sri Ishvari had brought from Gauda
she offered to Radha-Gopinatha.

274She prepared rice, vegetable dishes and many other foods
and fed Gopinatha together with Sri Radhika.

275She offered countless prayers to Radha-Gopinatha;
who could understand the ways of Ishvari?

276She went to Sri Govinda and Madanamohana;
seeing Them together with Sri Radhika, she refreshed her eyes.

277The three merciful Lords together with Sri Radhika
are truly the life and soul of the Gaudiyas.

278Thus [it is said] in the Sri Chaitanya-charitamrita, in the Antya-khanda:37
"Sri Sri Madanamohana together with Sri Radhika,
the feet of Sri Govinda together with Sri Radhika,

279Srila Gopinatha together with Sri Radhika —
these three are the life of the Gaudiyas, the lords of their life."

280How Sri Ishvari joyfully dwelt in Vrindavana —
that cannot be told with one mouth.

281The comings and goings of Sri Jahnava Ishvari —
all this the learned will describe in detail.

282How Ishvari went again to Vraja
is told in the Anuraga-valli and other books.38

283After some days Prabhu Virachandra
received permission from his mother to go to Vrindavana.

284At an auspicious moment he set out from Khardaha
and with his companions came to Saptagrama.

285In the house of a most virtuous merchant
he stayed two days, overwhelmed in kirtana.

286Having given the jewel of bhakti to the fallen and the suffering,
he came to Shantipura, rejoicing.

287With Krishna Mishra, the son of Prabhu Advaita,
he became supremely overwhelmed in sankirtana.

288Having told Krishna Mishra something in private — I do not know what —
he came to Ambika, taking his dear companions with him.

289What power have I to tell the joy that [was] there?
Coming to Navadvipa, he stayed [there] two days.

290The prema that Prabhu manifested in Nadiya
I can never describe with one mouth.

291From Navadvipa he soon set out for Shrikhanda;
Thakura Kanai came forward and led [him to his home].

292Thakura Kanai, the son of Sri Raghunandana —
it is impossible to tell what his loving deeds were like.

293Absorbed in sankirtana, the Prabhu gladdened him
and, having said something in private, set out for Yajigrama.

294Acharya Thakura with his associates came forward to meet him
and with great care took him to his house.

295There he was overwhelmed, absorbed in the rasa of talks about Krishna;
I do not know what he told the Acharya in private.

296From Yajigrama he went on to Kantaka-nagara;
the Acharya went along with him, together with his own associates.

297In Kantaka-nagara he stayed for one day;
there he was overwhelmed with prema day and night.

298Taking leave of Srinivasa Acharya, the Prabhu
went to the village of Sri Kheturi by way of Budhari.

299Sri Thakura Mahashaya — in what joy! —
came forward and brought Prabhu Virachandra.

300In sankirtana he danced in Gauranga's courtyard;
countless people came for the Prabhu's darshan.

301Having said something to Sri Thakura Mahashaya in private,
he set out joyfully for Vraja with his associates.

302On the way he showed mercy to a poor brahmana;
that brahmana became rich with the treasure of the jewel of bhakti.

303One brahmana, proud of his learning, held no one in regard;
crushing his pride, he made him full of bhakti.

304Displaying many wondrous pastimes on the way with his associates,
after some days he entered Mathura.

305The beauty of Prabhu Virachandra was extraordinary;
people ran to see [him] and could not stand still.

306Gazing at the Prabhu, people said to one another,
"Look — the son of Nityananda-Baladeva!"

307Someone said, "Can a human being have such beauty?"
Someone said, "He seems to be no human being at all."

308Someone said, "Look, what wonderful companions!
To see the radiance of them all is a delight to the eyes."

309Saying many such things, everyone stood gazing;
[the news of] Virachandra's arrival spread everywhere.

310Hearing of Virachandra's arrival in Vrindavana,
everyone comes forward to receive him:

311Sri Jiva Gosani, full of love for Sri Chaitanya;
Krishnadasa Kaviraja, the abode of virtues;

312the foremost disciple of Gadadhara Pandita Gosani,
the adhikari of Govinda, Sri Ananta Acharya;39

313his disciple Haridasa Pandita Gosani —
however much one tells, there is no end to the virtues of this adhikari of Govinda;

314Sri Govinda made known that He was subject to his love:
from him He begged rice with milk and ate it.

315Thus [it is said] in the Sadhana-dipika:
By the power of the Lord's command, Sri Rupa, the ocean of mercy,
entrusted the service of Sri Sri [Govinda] to my guru, named Haridasa.40

316Won over by his service, Sri Govinda, the son of Nanda,
the ocean of compassion, begs [from him] rice mixed with milk.

317The adhikari of the service of Sri Madana-gopala,
Gadadhara's disciple Krishnadasa Brahmachari;

318another disciple of Gadadhara Pandita Gosani,
Gosani Gopala Dasa, [invested] with high authority in service;41

319the adhikari of Sri Gopinatha, Sri Madhu Pandita,
known as a disciple of Gadadhara Pandita;

320Sri Madhu Pandita's fellow disciple Bhavananda,
whose great bliss is in the service of Gopinatha.

321Haridasa, Gopala, Sri Bhavananda and the others,
the adhikari of Govinda — all go joyfully.

322Kashishvara Gosani, renowned everywhere,
who has great affection for Sri Krishna Pandita;

323the disciples of Kashishvara Gosani, truly noble —
Govinda Gosani and Sri Yadava Acharya;

324Govinda, Yadava Acharya and all the others —
they all went in supreme joy.

325Everyone came, bringing Prabhu Virachandra with them;
the Vrajavasis rejoice at seeing the Prabhu.

326Who was not overwhelmed by the Prabhu's way of prema-bhakti?
All the Vaishnavas of Vraja sing his virtues.

327The darshan of Sri Govinda, Gopinatha and Madanamohana
Virachandra received together with everyone.

328He saw Sri Radha-vinoda and Radha-ramana;
seeing Radha-damodara, he filled his eyes with delight.

329Taking permission from Sri Bhugarbha, Sri Jiva Gosvami and the others,
he sets out to wander through the sacred forests.42

330Yadava Acharya and others went along with him;
he went to Madhuvana, Talavana, Kumudavana and Bahulavana.

331As he was going with everyone to Radha-kunda,
Sri Jiva Gosvami and others met him on that road.

332Surrounded by many Vaishnavas, the Prabhu
goes to the bank of the kunda and beholds wondrous beauty.

333Prabhu Gaurachandra, at the time of His wandering through the forests,
had sat by the kunda beneath a tamala tree.

334Going there, Virachandra became so full of prema
that everyone was astonished to see it.

335After some time, regaining composure, Prabhu Virachandra
felt great bliss at the sight of the two kundas.

336At Radha-kunda, Shyama-kunda and Govardhana Hill
he was utterly overwhelmed and danced in sankirtana.

337He fed the Vrajavasis with various foods
and stayed with everyone for five or six days.

338Sri Jiva, Sri Bhugarbha and the other bhagavatas
he sent off to go to Vrindavana.

339Although none of them could bear to leave him and go,
still they go, for the sake of his satisfaction.

340From Govardhana he went slowly
to the hut of Sri Krishnadasa Kaviraja.

341From there, after two days, [they] went to Vrindavana;
Krishnadasa Kaviraja went along [with them] as well.43

342Vasudeva, Uddhava, Yadava and several others
went with Prabhu Virachandra.44

343From Govardhana, seeing the places of Krishna's lila,
he set out with everyone for Kamyavana.

344Having bathed in Vimala-kunda and other kundas in Kamyavana,
he went with a greatly joyful heart to Vrishabhanupura.

345Vasudeva says to Prabhu Virachandra:
here is the abode of King Vrishabhanu.

346Coming here on various pretexts, Krishna
unseen beholds the sweetness of Radha's form.

347One day Krishna, sitting, thinks to Himself,
"How shall I get to Vrishabhanu's house?"

348For the festival of his daughter's birthday
Vrishabhanu sends Shridama to Nanda's house with an invitation.

349Shridama went and invited everyone;
everyone came to Vrishabhanu's house.

350Krishna in great bliss came here and stood still;
at a sign from a sakhi, Rai stayed in a secluded place.

351Radha and Krishna, both seeing each other's forms unnoticed,
were enchanted and could not turn their eyes away.

352Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Todi):
Knowing that the day of Radhika's birth has come,
no one in Vraja can keep composure.
Nanda, Yashoda and the others in great delight
come to Vrishabhanu's house.

353Vrishabhanu, having gone out to meet Nanda, comes into the house;
Krittika [comes in], bringing Yashoda.45
Scattering yogurt, turmeric and the rest in the courtyard,
the cowherds dance for joy.

354Instruments sound in many ways; in the uproar
no one hears with his ears what another says.
Finding the moment, Kala, unnoticed,
keeps gazing at Rai's face.46

355Moon-faced Radha keeps gazing at the beauty of Shyama's face,
unable to turn her eyes away.
Narahari says: I do not know what rasa
the two reveal as they look at each other.

356From Vrishabhanupura Prabhu Virachandra
entered Nandagrama with everyone.

357Vasudeva says, gazing at the Prabhu's face,
"Here there is great festivity on the day of Krishna's birth."

358Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Kamoda):
Queen Yashomati says to Nanda,
"Now is Krishna's birthday.
Invite and gather the kinsfolk —
this desire arises in my heart."

359Hearing this, Nanda Ghosha, pleased,
called Upananda's son
and sends him to Vrishabhanu's house,
giving him humble words to convey.

360Hearing, he went that very moment to Bhanu's house
and delivered the invitation.
Vrishabhanu with his people
sets out, taking various gifts.

361Joyful Queen Krittika, abounding in love,
taking Radhika with her,
was going gladly to Yashomati —
Yashoda met them on the way.

362With what affection the queen led them into the house
and seated them!
Vrishabhanu and Nanda met in joy;
auspicious sounds arose.

363In the town of Vraja, in house after house,
news of the festival spreads.
The gopis go lovingly to Nanda's home,
singing auspicious songs.

364Wearing various ornaments, the cowherds,
their hearts full of rasa with joy,
go to Nanda's house and pour out
yogurt, milk and ghee with turmeric.47

365With Nanda and the others, all dance in delight —
in it are waves of many kinds.
The instruments play; Ghanashyama again and again
sings of Nanda's great festival.48

366Again, raga Dhanashri:
On the day of Krishna's birth —
ah, what bliss in the house of Nanda!

367Seeing Radhika's face from afar,
from both of Krishna's unblinking eyes [tears] stream.

368Radhika cannot keep her composure,
gazing unseen at Shyama's moon-face.

369With the corner of her eye she signals to a sakhi:
"Among the elders — what can be done now?"

370Thinking and thinking, Vinodini
grew downcast; her whole body was soaked with sweat.

371Lalita, at that very moment,
devising a pretext, led Rai away to a secluded place.

372With a sign of her eyes Kundalata
sent Kanu to where Rai was.

373At the meeting of the two — great delight;
Narahari watches, staying at a distance with the sakhis.

374Having heard of the festivities of Krishna's birthday, with a joyful heart
he sees the places of Krishna's pastimes with his companions.

375At Sri Pavana-sarovara the Prabhu bathed;
having seen Khadiravana, he came to Javata.

376Joy at the sight of many places of Krishna's lila;
he went to Rama-ghat, where Rama performed the rasa.

377Singing the deeds of Baladeva, he danced;
seeing the place of Bhandiravata, he was filled with joy.

378Vasudeva says, "This is the place of Bhandiravata.
Sri Bhandiravata has disappeared [from sight]."49

379Hearing [this], Prabhu Virachandra, sitting in solitude,
contemplates within his mind the play that took place at Bhandira.

380Suddenly he sees Rama and Krishna, the two brothers,
sporting with the cowherd boys in that place.

381The beauty of Sri Bhandiravata is exceedingly enchanting;
seeing it, Prabhu Virachandra lost all composure at heart.

382Nanda-ghat, Chir-ghat; he went to Bhadravana;
he wandered through Bhandira and Sri Lohavana.

383Going with his companions to Sri Gokula-Mahavana,
he joyfully saw the birthplace of Krishna.

384Having seen at Raval the birthplace of Sri Radhika,
in Mathura he bathed at Sri Vishranti-ghat.

385Having seen the Shiva called Gokarna, he went to [the place of] Akrura;
in Vrindavana he entered the temple of Govinda.

386That day was the tithi of the eighth of the dark fortnight of Bhadra:
the resplendent abhisheka of Sri Govinda's birth.50

387Seeing all this, the people, in the joy of their hearts —
some say so much in sweet, gentle words:

388Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Mangala):
Today, at an auspicious moment, is the birth abhisheka:
on the throne shines the moon Govinda.
The countless graces of [His] body enchant the world;
[His] peerless form is an ocean of nectar.

389[His] face takes away all the pride of Manmatha;
seeing it, no one can keep composure.
Scattering curd, turmeric and the rest in the courtyard,
all dance with the sweetest grace.

390They sing abhisheka songs in many ways,
keeping the tala, and at this hearts overflow.
Mridangas and other instruments sound: "Drimi drimi,
ta drimiki drimi tadhik dhiya."51

391The lord of the gods, coming quite unseen,
rains flowers together with his host.
Again and again — cries of "Jaya, jaya!"; says
Ghanashyama, his heart rejoicing in delight.52

392Again, raga Kamoda:
Behold the abhisheka at the auspicious moment:
the Beloved of Gokula shines on the throne.

393Ah, I die! What sweetness of beauty!
It steals the very life of chaste women of good families.

394With what new fragrant substances
has someone rubbed this body? How can I hold my heart?

395Who lovingly dressed [Him] in yellow cloth?
Is it lightning flashing upon a cloud?

396With gorochana together with sandal,
who placed the tilaka on [His] forehead to enchant the world?

397Who tied [His] topknot with flowers?
The composure and the treasure of dharma of the whole world have fled.

398Who placed earrings in [His] ears?
How sweetly they swing — who is not bewitched by this?

399Who placed the jewelled necklace on [His] neck?
It has increased the burning of love-longing in the host of women.

400Who put ankle bells on [His] reddish feet?
Ringing "jhunu jhunu jhunu," they intoxicate the women.

401Ghanashyama offers himself [for Him];
at [His] tribhanga pose how many Kamadevas swoon!53

402Prabhu Virachandra's joy [grew] moment by moment
at the darshana of Madanamohana and Gopinatha.

403On the bright ashtami of Bhadra is Radhika's birth;
he sees the peerless beauty of its abhisheka.

404Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Kamoda):
How resplendent today is the auspicious abhisheka!
Radhika shines on the jewelled throne.

405Surpassing raw gold, [her] beauty glitters;
[her] moon-face takes away the pride of how many moons!

406The peerless glance of [her] eyes — a lovely splendour;
the grace of every limb entices the mind of the world.

407Who does not come to behold this beauty?
Having looked but once, they cannot turn their eyes away.

408On all four sides everyone raises cries of "Jaya, jaya!";
the sound of the instruments pervades the earth and the sky.

409With what eagerness the people dance — there is no counting them;
they scatter curd, milk and turmeric load upon load.

410Supreme merriment arises at every moment;
in such joy whose heart would not overflow?

411All the mendicants who came are fully satisfied;
the world is filled with [their] fame — so sings Narahari.

412Again, raga Kamoda:
How auspicious today is the abhisheka at the blessed moment!
Radhika shines on the jewelled throne.

413Look, look at that beauty, filling your eyes!
Which creator fashioned [her], and with what sweetness?

414A garland of golden lightning — what comparison is that for [her] beauty!
That moon-face steals the pride of the moon.

415What a sweet, sweet, sweet gentle smile!
It ceaselessly rains down nectar in heaps upon heaps.

416A glance that enchants the mind of the Enchanter of the world;
fish, khanjana birds and does give themselves up for [her] eyes.

417The sheen of [her] black hair darkens the world,
like a mass of clouds upon a crest of lightning.

418Touching [her] lip, the nose-ring shines beautifully;
[her] brows — she-serpents, or a row of bees?

419Madana swoons on seeing the radiance of [her] locks;
the beauty of [her] two arms surpasses golden lotus stalks.

420[Her] fingers gleam — champaka buds;
on the reddish palms, in the nails, mallika jasmine has blossomed.

421How sweet the curve of [her] neck! [Her] bosom is full;
[her] waist, exceedingly slender, puts the lion to shame.

422Peerless and graceful is the breadth of [her] hips;
[her] thighs, like inverted plantain trunks, are supremely beautiful.

423Beneath [her] lotus feet the dawn arises;
[they] shine in the heart of Narahari.

424Beholding Radhika's birth abhisheka,
Prabhu Virachandra cannot hold his heart.

425Staying some days in great bliss in Vrindavana,
he sets out for Gauda with his companions.

426How he took leave everywhere —
with one mouth I cannot relate any of it.

427At the time of departure everyone goes along with him;
having gone some distance, all weep.

428Prabhu Virachandra, bathed in tears,
bade farewell to all, saying so much.

429Prabhu Virachandra, summoning his composure,
went to Gauda by way of Mathura.

430Coming to Gauda, he wandered everywhere as before
and told everyone the account of Vrindavana.

431Constantly immersed in the bliss of sankirtana,
he went to Khardaha and bowed to his mother.

432The Prabhu's journey to Sri Vrindavana and back
I have told in brief; the learned will tell it in full.

433The nectarean deeds of Ganga and Virachandra54
I cannot expand, for fear of the book growing too long.

434Whoever hears all this with faith —
his bondage of worldly existence is removed without effort.

435Holding a straw between my teeth, I say again and again:
dive ceaselessly into the Bhakti-ratnakara.55

436Meditating on the feet of Srinivasa Acharya,
Narahari Dasa tells the Bhakti-ratnakara.

Thus in the Sri Bhakti-ratnakara ends the thirteenth wave, called "The Description of Srinivasa Acharya's Marriage and Other Events".

Notes

  1. দেখা এই হৈতে (dekhā ei haite) — literally "the meeting — from this"; apparently "we shall not see each other again": cf. 21, which tells of Ishana's departure.
  2. "Withdrew from sight" (সঙ্গোপন) — left this world, entered the eternal pastimes. Mauna-mudra — the vow of silence: the remaining devotees hardly speak.
  3. Sri Ishana Thakura — the servant in the Lord's (Shachi's) house in Navadvipa, who guided Srinivasa and his companions through Navadvipa (BR 12).
  4. Vira Hambira — the king of Vana-Vishnupura, a disciple of Srinivasa (BR 7).
  5. The Prabhu — here Srinivasa Acharya (cf. 40–41, "Acharya Prabhu"); in 42 and 45 "prabhu(s)" are his companions (Narottama and others), in 46 — "the Prabhu's associates."
  6. Ishta-goshthi — a conversation on spiritual subjects. The talks of Vira Hambira with Ramachandra Kaviraja; which book and which author are meant, the text does not say.
  7. The Deity of Radhika for Sri Gopinatha in Vrindavana, conceived by Jahnava (BR 11.715–717); the Gopinatha of 73 is this Deity.
  8. Kantaka-nagara is Katwa on the Ganga, where Mahaprabhu accepted sannyasa from Keshava Bharati; the ghat bears his name.
  9. Thakura Kanai is the son of Raghunandana of Shrikhanda.
  10. Jahnava's (Ishvari's) second journey to Vrindavana; the first is described in Taranga 11.
  11. "Gauranga" is the Deity of Gauranga in Kantaka-nagara (Katwa), served by Gadadhara Dasa; Yadunandana (109) is a servant of Gadadhara Dasa (cf. 9.558–598).
  12. Vira Hambira, as a king of robbers, had stolen the books of the Gosvamis that Srinivasa was bringing from Vrindavana, and Narottama then grieved over the loss (Taranga 7); afterwards the king became Srinivasa's disciple.
  13. Draupadi (Ishvari) is the first wife of Srinivasa Acharya (cf. Taranga 8).
  14. Khanda is Shrikhanda, Raghunandana's village.
  15. The Thakura is Raghunandana: never before had he told Srinivasa to come back quickly (cf. 146).
  16. That is, when he will depart from this world (cf. 180–183).
  17. The Thakura here is Srinivasa Acharya Thakura.
  18. The Sri Bhajanamrita is a work attributed to Narahari Sarakara Thakura of Shrikhanda; the verse number is not given in the text.
  19. Narahari Sarakara Thakura, Raghunandana's uncle and guru (also in 192).
  20. Shravana is a month of the rainy season (July–August). This is the day of Raghunandana's disappearance.
  21. "In youth" — Bengali kaiśore, in the age of kaishora; pauganda (192) is the age from five to ten.
  22. "At the parting": A (scan) reads গন্তুকালে (gantukāle, "at the time of going").
  23. Not the Gopalpura near Kheturi, but a village in Rarh (West Bengal).
  24. Gauranga-priya is Srinivasa's second wife; the first is Ishvari (Draupadi).
  25. Probably a hint at Advaita Acharya, who lived in Shantipura.
  26. So in A/B, "ব্রাহ্মণী" ("the brahmana's wife"); the 1960 edition has "ব্রাহ্মণ" — "the brahmana says".
  27. This is the Deity of Radhika that Jahnava had made and sent with Parameshvari Dasa to Sri Gopinatha in Vrindavana (11.715–717; 13.70–71). "The one we had brought": A (scan) reads যাঁরে (yā̃re, "whom").
  28. Thakurani ("the Mistress") is the earlier Deity of Radha, already present with Gopinatha; now Gopinatha stands between two Radhas (cf. 269–270).
  29. Tada-Atpur (in the text তড়া আঠপুর; in the 1960 ed. summary আটপুর) is a village in present-day Hooghly district (West Bengal), now Antpur; the Deity of Radha-Gopinatha installed by Parameshvari Dasa is worshipped there.
  30. Rajbalhat is a village in present-day Hooghly district; the Jhamatpur near it is apparently not the Jhamatpur that was the birthplace of Krishnadasa Kaviraja (Bardhaman district).
  31. Yadunandana Acharya of Jhamatpur is Virachandra's father-in-law (253); not to be confused with Yadunandana Chakravarti or Yadunandana of Kantaka-nagara (Taranga 9).
  32. Shrimati and Narayani are the wives of Virachandra; this Narayani is not the mother of Vrindavana Dasa.
  33. Payodhishayi ("He who lies on the ocean") is Kshirodakashayi Vishnu; a vyuha is an expansion.
  34. Shantanu is the king of the Mahabharata, the husband of the goddess Ganga. Nityananda's daughter bears the name Ganga in this birth as well.
  35. "Between the two Radhas" (মধ্যে রাধয়োঃ) is a dual: Gopinatha stands between two Deities of Radha (229–232, 269).
  36. "Remnants": by the scans, the 1960 edition reads দেবালভ্যফেলঃ (phelā, the remnants of the Deity's meal), A দেবালভ্যফেনঃ (phena, "foam"), apparently a misprint; translated after the 1960 edition.
  37. CC Antya 20 (the 1960 ed. gives 20.142–143). The quotation is from the Bengali verses of the Chaitanya-charitamrita.
  38. The Anuraga-valli is a Bengali biography of Srinivasa Acharya written by Manohara Dasa (late 17th c.).
  39. Adhikari — the person in charge of a Deity's service.
